sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Merey. Merey data (from Gravina's own unpublished lexicon / 'Merey Phonology Sketch') used in sec. 5.3.1 Mofu group (both palatalization and labialization prosodies present) and Table 171 p.329 (labialization prosody in Merey); the reconstruction explicitly excludes 'tone or stress' (p.1).

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2007. The Verb Phrase in Merey. Yaoundé: SIL / Ministère de la Recherche Scientifique et de l'Innovation. ii+19 pp. (SIL archives 47663; the sole Glottolog descriptive reference).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 2.5 Prosody (palatalisation/labialisation of verb roots); sec. 2.6 'Underlying tone' (printed p.4 = PDF p.8): 'Verbs carry a single underlying tone, either High, Mid or Low'; completive/incompletive/anterior/subjunctive distinguished by prefix tone. The words stress/accent do not occur.

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3.2 'Les tons' (PDF p.7): three tones (haut, moyen, bas), tone mostly left unmarked, circumflex marks the subjunctive prefix; sec. 2.2 two basic vowels /a/, /ə/ plus palatalisation/labialisation prosodies; sec. 3.1.11 phrase-medial /a/ -> [ə] in closed syllables. No mention of stress or accent d'intensité.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. n.d. [c. 2001-2007]. Merey Phonology Sketch. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon (unpublished manuscript; cited in Gravina 2014 bibliography and as the Merey source in his Mofu-group survey).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only dedicated phonology of Merey known to exist; Gravina's parallel Mbuko phonology (1999) has a 'Metrical Phonology / The Metrical System' chapter with an explicit stress statement, so this sketch very likely contains one for Merey. Not in the SIL archives listing; would have to be requested from the author or SIL Cameroon (Yaoundé/Maroua library).
